_comment: The Meadows mix. Read by scripts/audio/audio_manager.gd and scripts/audio/world_audio.gd. CLAUDE.md's rule is that a number anyone could argue about lives in data and something actually reads it -- this file is the audio half of what data/config/art.json is for the lighting. The bus VOLUMES are not here: they are in default_bus_layout.tres, because the engine loads that before any config reader runs (see tools/audio/make_bus_layout.gd).
_comment_assets: Every path below is generated by tools/audio/gen_*.py and committed. Nothing here is sourced; see docs/specs/ASSET_LEDGER.md's row for assets/audio/.

buses._comment: The buses the settings screen offers a slider for, in the order it draws them. `default_db` mirrors default_bus_layout.tres and is the 100% point -- a player slider scales relative to it, so a fresh install matches the authored mix exactly. `min_db` is the value at 0%, below which the bus is muted outright rather than left inaudibly quiet.

ambience._comment: Eight layers, mixed live at per-band gains. See tools/audio/gen_ambience.py's header for why this is layers rather than ten finished beds. A gain of 0 means the layer's player is stopped entirely, so a band pays no CPU for layers it does not use.
ambience._comment_fade: Seconds to cross from one band's mix to the next, and from day to night. Long: a band boundary is a line on a map, not a door, and a player walking along one must not hear the mix flapping. 6s is about two of the player's strides per dB at these gain deltas.
ambience._comment_bands: Per-band, per-time layer gains, 0..1, applied on top of each layer's own authored level. Keys are the band ids in data/config/bands/ and scripts/data/band_content.gd's BANDS. `_identity` is a note to the next person about what this band is supposed to sound like, so a later edit can tell a deliberate choice from a typo.

band1_lower_meadows._identity: Home. Open, gentle, pastoral -- the safest place in the chapter and the one the player must want to come back to. Birds carry it by day; nothing here is threatening at night either, just quieter.

band2_stone_and_root._identity: Dry, hollow, half-enclosed. The character here is ABSENCE -- the air goes away and the birds thin out. If this band sounds busy, it is wrong.

band3_the_river_lock._identity: Water, and lots of it. The river is the loudest natural thing in the chapter and the one landmark a player can navigate to by ear alone.

band4_upper_meadows_ironwood._identity: Higher, windier, under a canopy. Creaking timber says 'big old trees' more economically than any amount of leaf rustle.

band5_stronghold_approach._identity: Exposed and wrong. The only band with an unnatural layer in it: Team Tether's machinery is audible before it is visible, which is the point.

ambience._comment_interior: Indoors, the outside world is muffled rather than silenced. One gain multiplier applied to every layer while the player is inside a structure.

footsteps._comment: Stride timing is derived from speed rather than from an animation event: the player rig's walk cycle is not currently frame-tagged, and a distance-based stride stays in step with sprint, slopes and the movement config's own speeds without a second source of truth. `stride_metres` is how far the player travels between steps at a walk.
footsteps._comment_sprint: Sprinting does not just play the same step faster -- it shortens the stride AND lifts the level, which is what running actually sounds like.
footsteps._comment_pitch: Random pitch per step, on top of the 3-4 generated variants. Small: past about +/-8% a footstep starts to read as a different-sized creature.
footsteps._comment_surfaces: Which sound set plays on what. Resolution order is water -> structure -> band default; see world_audio.gd::_surface_for. This is deliberately COARSE -- the terrain does not carry a per-texture material id, and inventing one for footsteps alone would be a terrain change this lane has no business making. Recorded as a known limitation rather than hidden.
footsteps._comment_structure: Substrings matched against the name of the body the player is standing on. A built floor, a house interior and a bridge deck are all wood; nothing else matches, so the band default wins.
footsteps._comment_water: How far the player's feet may sit below the water surface and still be walking IN it rather than swimming under it. Above this depth the surface is water; deeper, water.gd's own submersion hazard has taken over and footsteps are not the sound that matters.

sfx._comment: dir + the variant sets. A name with variants is stored as `<name>_1..N` on disk and played by its base name; AudioManager.play resolves that and refuses to repeat the variant it played last.
sfx._comment_pool: How many one-shot players exist. A fight with three creatures, footsteps and an ambience change underneath needs more than a handful; 16 is well clear of anything observed and costs almost nothing while idle.
sfx._comment_max_distance: AudioStreamPlayer3D falloff for world sounds. 40m matches the distance at which a creature is still a readable silhouette.
sfx._comment_gather: Which sound a harvest makes, keyed by the tool the resource needs (autoload/item_db.gd's `gathered_with`). Keyed off the TOOL rather than the resource id so a new berry bush or a new ore needs no audio change -- it inherits from whatever swings at it. `` (empty) is the bare-handed case, which is picking something.

combat._comment: Which sound answers which of combat_manager.gd's existing signals. Nothing in the combat code was changed to add audio -- these are all signals it already emitted. `effectiveness` keys are type_chart.gd's classify() values.
combat._comment_shake: Each successive orb shake plays a semitone higher. Three rising clicks is a question; three identical ones is a stutter.

progression._comment: PROGRESSION-VISIBLE (docs/prompts/73 §2.2, D74). Which generated sfx answers each Moment on the progression feed -- the cue ids data/config/progression_feedback.json's `sound_cues` names resolve here to a file under sfx.dir, the same indirection `combat.effectiveness_sound` uses. Played on the UI bus by the world HUD's moment banner (playground_hud.gd), so the level-up is heard at one level wherever the creature stands. Ticks (an ordinary xp or bond credit) are deliberately silent: the directive's own rule is that ordinary gains are subtle and milestones are loud.

creatures._comment: Voice ARCHETYPES, not one file per species. Each species names an archetype plus a pitch, and the archetype's clip is played at that pitch -- so twenty species cost four files. See tools/audio/gen_creatures.py. A species with no entry falls back to `default`.
creatures._comment_idle: Idle calls are rare on purpose. A creature that vocalises every few seconds stops being alive and starts being a car alarm; the interval is randomised per creature so a group does not chorus.
creatures._comment_species: Pitch is the main differentiator within an archetype and is keyed off size: bigger creature, lower voice. Where a species is not listed the default applies, which is audible but generic -- that is a gap to fill, not a design.

music._comment: One track at a time, crossfaded. `priority` decides what wins when two states are true at once -- a fight inside the village is a fight. The Warden and the release ceremony are the chapter's two structural beats (docs/GAME_VISION.md) and outrank everything.
music._comment_silence: Music does not play continuously. Exploration music that never stops is the fastest way to make a 3-4 hour chapter exhausting, so the exploration bed plays in stretches with real gaps between them, and the ambience carries the rest. Seconds of music, then seconds of silence.
music._comment_village_radius: Metres from the village centre at which the village cue takes over. The village is the chapter's rest beat and it should be audible as one before it is visible as one.
